draft.title: Use the provider's hosted payment page for bike rentals
draft.choice: Send riders to the payment provider's hosted payment page instead of building our own card form.
reasons: Keeps card data off our servers and out of PCI scope.

conditions.label: Checkout abandonment
conditions.trigger: A capture reports checkout abandonment on the hosted payment page above 25%, measured over at least seven consecutive days.
conditions.action: Reconsider building an embedded card form.

conditions.label: Payment flow review
conditions.action: Compare hosted page fees and conversion against an embedded form.

steps.text: Funnel for 1-7 November: checkout abandonment on the hosted payment page reached 31%.
Checkout abandonment on the hosted payment page spiked to 41% during Sunday's one-hour outage; the seven-day figure stayed at 17%.
From 8 to 14 November, 2,300 riders reached the card-entry screen our payment provider hosts, and 690 of them left without paying.
Funnel for 1-7 November: checkout abandonment on the hosted payment page reached 31%.

draft.title: Render delivery maps from vector tiles on the device
draft.choice: Draw the courier-tracking map from vector tiles on the phone rather than downloading pre-rendered raster images.
reasons: Smaller downloads and crisp street labels at every zoom level.

conditions.label: Low-end map smoothness
conditions.trigger: A capture reports vector tiles rendering below 30 fps on a supported low-end phone.
conditions.action: Reconsider falling back to raster tiles on low-end phones.

changes.trigger: A capture reports vector tiles rendering below 24 fps during panning on a supported low-end phone.

steps.text: On the cheapest supported phone, vector tiles rendered at 27 fps while panning across the city centre.
After the label-collision update, vector tiles dropped to 19 fps during panning on the cheapest supported phone.
With the label cache enabled, vector tiles held a steady 58 fps during panning on every supported low-end phone.
A courier's budget handset from the supported list was screen-recorded today: while she dragged the live map around the depot, the map the phone draws itself refreshed only about 14 times a second.

draft.title: Use email magic links for team-chat sign-in
draft.choice: Sign users in with one-time email links instead of passwords.
reasons: No password storage and no reset flow to build.

conditions.label: Slow sign-in emails
conditions.trigger: A capture reports at least 5% of magic link emails arriving more than two minutes after they were requested, measured over a full day or longer.
conditions.action: Reconsider adding password sign-in or one-time codes.

conditions.label: Sign-in method review
conditions.action: Check sign-in completion rates before the enterprise pilot.

steps.text: Mail provider logs for 8 November: 7% of magic link emails were delayed by more than two minutes, with delivery taking up to nine minutes.
Mail provider logs for 9 November: every magic link email arrived within 20 seconds of the request; none were delayed.
Magic link delivery on 10 November: 12% of the emails were delayed by more than two minutes.
Across all of 11 November, 140 of 1,900 one-time sign-in messages reached inboxes three or more minutes after people pressed 'Email me a link'.
Mail provider logs for 13 November: 9% of magic link emails were delayed past two minutes.

draft.title: Upload inspection photos only on Wi-Fi
draft.choice: Queue inspection reports and photos on the tablet and upload them only over Wi-Fi, never over mobile data.
reasons: Photo sets are large and inspectors' data plans are capped.
alternatives: Upload over mobile data with heavy compression

conditions.label: Stale reports
conditions.trigger: A capture reports a finished inspection report waiting in the upload queue for more than 24 hours because no Wi-Fi was available.
conditions.action: Reconsider allowing compressed uploads over mobile data.

changes.trigger: A capture reports a finished inspection report waiting in the upload queue for more than 48 hours because no Wi-Fi was available.

steps.text: A finished report from the river crossing sat in the upload queue for 30 hours because the site had no Wi-Fi.
The upload queue grew to 37 reports during a six-hour office Wi-Fi outage; all of them were sent within 40 minutes of it coming back.
Two finished reports were stuck in the upload queue for 60 hours with no Wi-Fi at the dam site.
The quarry inspection report was stuck in the upload queue for 52 hours because the quarry has no Wi-Fi.
An inspector working the ridge mine had no wireless network for three days, so her completed report stayed on the tablet and only reached the server on the fourth morning.

draft.title: Keep invoicing logs for 14 days
draft.choice: Delete invoicing-service application logs after 14 days.
reasons: Logs contain customer names and amounts; shorter retention means less exposure.

conditions.label: Retention review
conditions.action: Check whether 14 days still covers billing disputes.

conditions.label: Privacy audit
conditions.action: Confirm the deletion jobs ran and no copies remain in backups.

conditions.label: Blocked investigations
conditions.trigger: A capture reports a support investigation that could not be completed because the logs it needed had already been deleted under retention.
conditions.action: Reconsider extending retention for billing events.

steps.text: Support ticket 4471: the investigation could not be finished because the logs for the disputed invoice were 19 days old and already deleted under retention.
All 212 support tickets closed in October were fully investigated; none needed logs older than the 14-day retention window.
Support ticket 4510 needed logs from 20 days ago; they were gone under retention, but the agent completed the investigation using the invoice audit trail instead.

draft.title: Compute recipe nutrition in the browser with WebAssembly
draft.choice: Run the nutrition calculator client-side as a WebAssembly module instead of calling a server API.
reasons: Works offline in the kitchen and costs nothing per request.

conditions.label: Slow calculation
conditions.trigger: A capture reports the nutrition calculator taking more than 2 seconds for a single recipe on a supported device.
conditions.action: Reconsider moving the calculation to a server API.

conditions.label: Client compute review
conditions.action: Check bundle size and device coverage of the WebAssembly module.

steps.text: The WebAssembly nutrition calculator took 3.4 seconds for a 40-ingredient stew on the oldest supported tablet.
The WebAssembly nutrition calculator took 3.4 seconds for a 40-ingredient stew on the oldest supported tablet.

changes.trigger: A capture reports the nutrition calculator taking more than 5 seconds for a single recipe on a supported device.

steps.text: The nutrition calculator needed 3.9 seconds for the holiday roast recipe on a supported Chromebook.
The Wasm nutrition calculator took 7.2 seconds for a single recipe on the slowest supported phone.

draft.title: Render event tickets as PDF on the server
draft.choice: Generate each conference ticket as a server-rendered PDF with a QR code.
reasons: One format that prints and opens the same everywhere.

conditions.label: Unreadable tickets
conditions.trigger: A capture reports venue scanners failing to read the QR code on more than 2% of printed PDF tickets at a single event.
conditions.action: Reconsider adding wallet passes or changing the QR code size.

conditions.label: Ticket format review
conditions.action: Check whether attendees still print tickets.

draft.choice: Host the web client, mobile client and shared libraries in a single repository.
reasons: Shared types change in one commit across all clients.
alternatives: Separate repositories with a published shared package
